og.title: ClinicalSync — Clinical continuity for cardiovascular units
og.description: Standardizes SBAR handover, records vital signs in seconds, and keeps a record of who did what and when.

hero.title: Shift information should not depend on anyone's memory
hero.subtitle: ClinicalSync standardizes shift handover with SBAR, lets staff record vital signs and clinical events in seconds, and keeps a record of who did what and when.

problem.title: What gets lost between one shift and the next
problem.intro: In cardiovascular units, patient information is spread across the hospital system, bedside monitors, paper notes, and whatever is passed on verbally during handover. That dispersion causes duplicate records, delays when looking things up, and omissions at the most sensitive moment of the process.

card1.title: Duplicate recording
card1.text: Staff write on paper during care and transcribe into the system at the end of the shift.

card2.title: Loss at handover
card2.text: Unstructured verbal handover leaves out information the incoming shift needs.

card3.title: No traceability
card3.text: It is not always possible to determine who recorded a given entry, or when.

problem.finding: According to interviews our team conducted with cardiovascular nursing staff, documentation takes up roughly a quarter of the shift.
problem.context: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in Peru according to the Ministry of Health, and the ENDES 2024 survey reports that 14.2% of Peruvians over 15 have high blood pressure.

step1.title: Receive your shift
step1.text: Review the outgoing team's handover in SBAR format and confirm you received it.

step2.title: Record during care
step2.text: Vital signs, administered medication and clinical events, in a few steps and from whichever device you have at hand.

step3.title: Carry out and confirm orders
step3.text: Active medical orders stay visible, and their completion is recorded with the responsible staff member and time.

step4.title: Hand over without omissions
step4.text: The handover is assembled from what you already recorded during the shift.

f1.title: Structured SBAR handover
f1.text: A form with the four required sections and confirmation of receipt by the incoming shift.

f2.title: Vital signs recording
f2.text: Quick capture linked to the patient, with automatic date, time and responsible staff member.

f3.title: Clinical events
f3.text: Documentation of what matters during the shift, flagged by criticality.

f4.title: Orders and completion
f4.text: The full cycle between what is ordered and what is actually carried out.

f5.title: Clinical summary
f5.text: A consolidated view of the patient's recent progress.

f6.title: Audit trail
f6.text: A searchable history of actions, responsible staff and timestamps.

benefits.title: Depending on your role in the unit

nursing.title: Nursing staff
nursing.text: Fewer steps to record, no transcribing from paper into the system, and a handover that does not rely on remembering everything.

physician.title: Specialist physicians
physician.text: The patient's status in a single view, without gathering data from several sources, and with certainty about where each entry came from.

institution.title: Healthcare institutions
institution.text: Full traceability of care and continuity between shifts, without replacing the existing hospital system.

q1.q: Does ClinicalSync replace my institution's system?
q1.a: No. It is a complementary tool focused on the day-to-day work of the cardiovascular shift. It runs alongside the existing hospital system.

q2.q: What security measures does the design consider?
q2.a: The design includes role-based authentication, access control by assigned shift, and an audit log that only accepts insertions, so no recorded action can be altered afterwards.

q3.q: What do I need to use it?
q3.a: A web browser. It works on desktop, tablet and phone, so staff can record at the patient's bedside.

q4.q: How is it different from an electronic health record?
q4.a: In scope. The health record holds the institutional record of the patient; ClinicalSync solves shift continuity: the handover, immediate recording and traceability.
